original_question: Consider the linear parabolic stochastic PDE system partial u_i / partial t (t, x) = partial^2 u_i / partial x^2 (t, x) + B-hat_i(t, x) with reasonable boundary conditions, where B-dot_1, ..., B-dot_d are independent space-time white noises. Is there a theory of slices along fixed times t for this parabolic system that parallels the Brownian-sheet slice results proved in the paper, such as the analysis of zeros, double points, and exceptional slices?
target_in_paper: Section 8.4, Open Problem 6: for the additive linear parabolic SPDE system driven by d independent space-time white noises, determine whether one can analyze the time-slices of the solution u in a way analogous to the Brownian-sheet slice results proved earlier in the paper. ([math.utah.edu](https://www.math.utah.edu/~davar/PPT/SLICES/SlicesFinal.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper on the core SPDE, the independence of the d driving noises, the focus on slices indexed by fixed times t, and the intended analogy with the Brownian-sheet slice theory. It also points to the right earlier phenomena—zeros, double points, and exceptional slice behavior—that make the phrase “analogous to the results of the present paper” concrete. ([math.utah.edu](https://www.math.utah.edu/~davar/PPT/SLICES/SlicesFinal.pdf))
missing_details: The paper poses this as an open problem about parabolic SPDEs in the additive linear case only; it is not the nonlinear or multiplicative-noise problem from the immediately preceding Open Problem 5. ([math.utah.edu](https://www.math.utah.edu/~davar/PPT/SLICES/SlicesFinal.pdf))

A fully stand-alone version should state that u=(u_1,...,u_d) is d-dimensional, with components satisfying ∂_t u_i(t,x)=∂_x^2 u_i(t,x)+ξ_i(t,x), i=1,...,d, where ξ_1,...,ξ_d are independent two-parameter (space-time) white noises. ([math.utah.edu](https://www.math.utah.edu/~davar/PPT/SLICES/SlicesFinal.pdf))

The paper deliberately does not fix a specific spatial domain or initial/boundary data beyond saying “reasonable boundary conditions,” so a faithful rewrite should keep that deliberate flexibility rather than add extra hypotheses. ([math.utah.edu](https://www.math.utah.edu/~davar/PPT/SLICES/SlicesFinal.pdf))

The notion of “slice” should be made explicit as freezing t and viewing the spatial profile x↦u(t,x), mirroring the paper’s earlier definition of Brownian-sheet slices obtained by freezing one parameter and varying the other. ([math.utah.edu](https://www.math.utah.edu/~davar/PPT/SLICES/SlicesFinal.pdf))

To stay closest to the paper, the requested analogy should be tied to the paper’s actual slice results: zeros of slices (Theorems 1.1 and 1.2, plus Open Problem 1), double points of slices (Theorem 1.4, Theorem 5.1, and Open Problems 2–3), and exceptional escape behavior of slices (Theorem 1.6). ([math.utah.edu](https://www.math.utah.edu/~davar/PPT/SLICES/SlicesFinal.pdf))
refined_question: For the d-vector solution u=(u_1,...,u_d) of the additive linear one-dimensional parabolic SPDE system ∂_t u_i(t,x)=∂_x^2 u_i(t,x)+ξ_i(t,x), i=1,...,d, where ξ_1,...,ξ_d are independent space-time white noises and the boundary conditions are left “reasonable” in the sense of the paper, can one develop a theory of the time-slices x↦u(t,x), as t varies, that is directly analogous to the Brownian-sheet slice theory established earlier in the paper—specifically, analogues of the paper’s results on slice zeros, slice double points, and exceptional slice behavior? ([math.utah.edu](https://www.math.utah.edu/~davar/PPT/SLICES/SlicesFinal.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 8.4 rather than any earlier Brownian-sheet theorem: its equation, its reference to fixed-time slices, and its request for a Brownian-sheet-type analogue match Open Problem 6 almost verbatim in substance. The main sharpening is to mark that the paper asks this only in the additive linear parabolic setting, while the intended benchmark for “analogous” comes from the paper’s earlier slice results on zeros, double points, and exceptional escape phenomena. The author also remarks that some results along these lines were expected in forthcoming work with Dalang and Nualart. ([math.utah.edu](https://www.math.utah.edu/~davar/PPT/SLICES/SlicesFinal.pdf))
